title: BlueBridge co-sell pipeline prioritization + risk playbook
next_steps: Maya to send updated co-sell one-pager and pricing bands by 2027-03-07
Liam to provision benchmark run for BBH pilot by 2027-03-10
Karen to share BlueBridge compliance checklist and SOC 2 contact by 2027-03-08
action_items: Maya: Send co-sell one-pager + pricing bands - due 2027-03-07
Liam: Setup Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark run (3 workloads) - due 2027-03-10
Karen: Share SOC 2 contact and compliance checklist - due 2027-03-08
summary: Quarterly cadence check-in to prioritize joint accounts for co-sell. Discussed three priority mid-market healthcare accounts, evaluated technical blockers (VPC requirements, data residency), pricing bands for reserved capacity, and a risk playbook for churn/compete scenarios. Agreed to run a short Dedicated-hosted benchmark and share security artifacts. Next steps and owners assigned.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-03-04 15:00 UTC; Duration: 48 minutes; Attendees: Maya, Liam, Sofia (Redwood) - Rajiv, Karen, Ethan (BlueBridge)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Rajiv Menon: Rajiv here. Karen?
[00:12] Karen Liu: Karen here. Ethan on the line as well.
[00:16] Liam Patel: Liam here, hi.
[00:18] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia in the background.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great, scope for today: triage the co-sell pipeline, pick top 3 accounts to focus on this quarter, and review the risk playbook if we hit renewals or competitor motions.

[02:05] Rajiv Menon: Quick note from my side, we've got heavy interest from two payer clients and one hospital group, but both payers are very strict on VPC and data-in-transit, so wanna understand how Redwood handles private deployments.
[02:30] Liam Patel: Yeah we can do Private (VPC) or Dedicated — Dedicated is our reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and you can opt into VPC peering for a private network path. There's a config matrix we'll share.

[04:01] Karen Liu: On vendor selection we've got MajorCloudAI in the running, they gave a deep discount on inference but no private deploy was available. That worries our security team. How does Redwood compare on unit economics?
[04:25] Maya Chen: Good question. For hosted usage, per-token costs are competitive; but for larger steady workloads we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity which drops unit cost. We'll send pricing bands — there's also Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization) to save another 20-30% in many cases.

[06:10] Ethan Ross: Procurement note: we need standard terms and evidence of SOC 2 type II. Do you have a single contact we can ping?
[06:25] Sofia Alvarez: I'll share our security pack and SOC 2 contact. We also have KMS/HSM integration notes.

[07:40] Rajiv Menon: For the pilot we wanna run three workloads: triage triage I mean — clinical note summarization, patient intake triage, and a reranking/triage for search. We care about latency end-to-end under 250ms p95 for short prompts. Is that realistic?
[08:05] Liam Patel: For p95 250ms on short prompts, hosted with a low-latency model can hit that; if you need strict isolation and the same latency, Dedicated with pinned model version and region will be more predictable. We'll test with sample sequences.

[09:30] Maya Chen: Ok let's pivot to account prioritization. We propose: 1) Meridian Payers (likely close, legal windows Q2), 2) Northwell-ish hospital group (longer but high ACV), 3) Tidemark Insurers (fits mid-market). Karen, does that map to your list?
[09:55] Karen Liu: Pretty close. I'd swap Meridian and Tidemark priority based on exec sponsor alignment — Meridian stalled a bit on procurement last week.

[11:02] Rajiv Menon: Can Redwood support data residency within eu-west-1 and us-east-1 only? Some of our clients require EU-only.
[11:20] Liam Patel: Yes, we have region pinning and Private deployments can be constrained to a region. There's also audit logs and retention controls. We'll add the exact policy doc.

[12:45] Maya Chen: Let's discuss the risk playbook — if a competitor pushes a price cut or bespoke integration, how do we respond? Proposed steps: 1) Rapid POC offer (two-week benchmark), 2) joint exec sponsorship push, 3) competitive displacement credits. Thoughts?
[13:10] Karen Liu: The two-week benchmark is crucial. If we can show performance/econ delta in 10 business days, that's persuasive. Also the SOC2 and onboarding velocity matter.

[14:40] Liam Patel: For the benchmark we'll do three experiments: latency test under steady-state qps, cost-per-1000-tokens delta with quantized model, and failure/fallback scenarios. We'll provide raw logs and sample prompts.

[16:05] Rajiv Menon: One caveat: several of our clients insist on no external callouts for PII. Can you run the benchmark in an air-gapped or masked dataset?
[16:20] Liam Patel: We can run on synthetic/masked datasets. For Private on-prem options we can do an air-gapped deploy but that increases lead time. For the pilot, masked synthetic will be fastest.

[17:50] Ethan Ross: Contractually we need indemnity language and a data processing addendum. We'll send a standard DPA.
[18:05] Maya Chen: Noted — we'll loop in legal. We have standard DPA templates and enterprise SOW structures.

[19:35] Sofia Alvarez: Quick co-sell motion detail: Redwood can provide MDF credits for qualified joint pipeline, and we can do joint customer-facing webinars. For these mid-market deals, co-marketing helped close earlier deals.
[20:00] Karen Liu: That helps. Also curious about lead routing — how are inbound leads attributed when both teams engage?
[20:18] Maya Chen: We use a joint lead registration form and qualify via our partner portal. We can set up a deal routing rule: partner originates = partner gets referral credit; if Redwood introduces we follow standard attribution. We'll share the portal link.

[21:45] Rajiv Menon: Regarding observability, can we get token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards for the pilot? It's important for our engineering team to verify SLOs.
[22:05] Liam Patel: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route metrics, token cost breakdowns, and trace hooks. For Dedicated we can also push logs to your SIEM. We'll draft sample dashboards.

[23:40] Maya Chen: Let's surface a sample timeline: Week 0: finalize SOW and NDA; Week 1-2: benchmark runs; Week 3: joint exec review and pricing; Week 4: kickoff pilot integration. Does that cadence work?
[24:02] Karen Liu: Sounds good if procurement can move quickly.

[25:30] Rajiv Menon: I'm worried about fallback handling if the Dedicated pool has maintenance. Any graceful degradation path?
[25:45] Liam Patel: Yes we provide smart routing and automated fallback to a compatible hosted model variant to keep apps up, though with different unit economics. We can surface fallback events in the dashboard.

[27:10] Ethan Ross: Can you summarize the cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for a steady 24/7 workload? Ballpark numbers help procurement.
[27:30] Maya Chen: Ballpark — hosted per-token is higher but no commit (~x). Dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit cost by ~35-50% depending on GPU class and batching. We'll send a tailored costing sheet after we see the sample qps and sequence lengths.

[29:00] Karen Liu: Competitor behavior: MajorCloudAI offered a steep discount but had no SOC 2 guidance; FastServe Labs promised integration work but had higher latency. We need to highlight Redwood's reliability story.
[29:20] Sofia Alvarez: We'll prepare a one-pager: reliability, observability, fallback playbook, and case studies.

[31:10] Rajiv Menon: On quantization, will that affect output accuracy for clinical summarization? Our clinicians are sensitive.
[31:30] Liam Patel: Good question. We recommend accuracy-sensitive models run at higher precision; quantization profiles can be tuned per workload. For clinical summarization we'll test both FP16 and int8 and include evaluation metrics (ROUGE, clinician review).

[33:05] Maya Chen: Ok action items recap: Maya send co-sell one-pager and pricing bands; Liam run benchmark and share results; Sofia share MDF/partner portal details; Karen share compliance checklist and SOC contact; Rajiv to provide sample prompts.

[34:10] Ethan Ross: About the benchmark, can we request RBAC and SSO test accounts? We want to test SAML SSO flow during integration.
[34:28] Liam Patel: Absolutely — we'll enable a test SAML SSO and RBAC roles in the staging console.

[36:00] Karen Liu: A small ask — for executive messaging we'll need a joint slide with joint value prop and logos. Can Redwood provide an editable slide?
[36:15] Maya Chen: Yes we'll provide a co-brandable deck.

[37:40] Rajiv Menon: Timeline caveat: if procurement drags beyond end of March, we may need to push pilots. Any flexibility?
[37:55] Maya Chen: We can be flexible but reserved capacity discounts have limited windows. If procurement delays, we can still run hosted pilots to keep momentum.

[39:10] Sofia Alvarez: Risk playbook addendum — if a competitive lower-price motion shows up, recommended steps: fast benchmark, joint exec outreach, limited promotional credits for retention. We'll codify this in a one-page playbook.

[40:30] Ethan Ross: Who's the exec sponsor on Redwood side? That often helps move internal stakeholders.
[40:40] Maya Chen: I'll be the AE sponsor and Sofia will handle partner ops; we can get an SE exec if needed.

[42:05] Rajiv Menon: Any regulatory certifications beyond SOC2 we should be aware of? ISO? HIPAA?
[42:20] Liam Patel: We have HIPAA controls for BAA engagements and can discuss ISO in enterprise deals; HIPAA work often goes hand-in-hand with Private deployments. We'll include the HIPAA readiness doc.

[44:00] Karen Liu: Last thing — pipeline prioritization: we'll finalize top 3 list by Monday and share contact details for each account.
[44:15] Maya Chen: Great. For transparency we'll log each joint account in the partner portal with expected close date and red flags.

[45:30] Ethan Ross: Procurement will follow up with contract redlines; expect email.
[45:40] Maya Chen: Perfect. Any other questions?
[46:05] Rajiv Menon: No, thanks for the time.
[46:10] Karen Liu: Thanks all.
[46:15] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll send notes and artifacts later today. Meeting close.

End of transcript.
